skills.name: Incident and Component Data Model

testcases.name: severity enum has exactly 3 documented severities
incident state enum has exactly 4 documented states in order

skills.capability: Defines the shared schema (SQLite tables or JSON seed-store shape) for Incidents, Components, and state-transition history that all downstream endpoints and features consume.
skills.prompt_template: You are a backend data-modeling agent. Define the canonical Incident schema (id, title, severity, affectedComponents, summary, state, stateHistory[]) and Component schema (id, name, healthState, uptimePercent) as either SQLite table migrations or a typed JSON store shape. Export shared enum constants for severities and incident states so every other module references the same source of truth. Do not implement business logic or endpoints here — this skill only produces the schema/migration and constant exports.
acceptance_criteria: Schema module exports the exact set of 3 severities (SEV1, SEV2, SEV3)
Schema module exports the exact set of 4 incident states (open, investigating, identified, resolved) in workflow order
Database/store initializes required tables or collections automatically on process startup with no manual migration step

skills.name: Deterministic Seed Data Loader
skills.capability: Builds a fixed, deterministic seed dataset of incidents and components covering all 4 states and all 3 severities, auto-loaded on fresh install.
skills.prompt_template: You are a backend seeding agent. Using the schema from SKILL_001, author a deterministic fixture dataset (no random IDs, no Date.now()) of multiple components and incidents that together cover all 4 incident states and all 3 severities. Wire it to load automatically the first time the app boots against an empty database/store, with no CLI command or manual step required. Keep timestamps as fixed ISO strings so tests relying on this data are reproducible.
acceptance_criteria: Seed dataset contains at least one incident in each of the 4 defined states
Seed dataset contains at least one incident of each of the 3 defined severities across multiple components
Seeding executes automatically on a fresh install/empty database with zero manual setup steps

skills.name: Deterministic Uptime Calculation Engine

testcases.name: uptime percent for fixed downtime and period

skills.capability: Implements a pure, injectable-timestamp function computing uptime % as (time-in-non-operational-state / total period), with no reliance on Date.now().
skills.prompt_template: You are a backend algorithms agent. Implement calculateUptime as a pure function that takes downtime duration and total period duration (or explicit start/end boundaries) as arguments and returns an uptime percentage, never calling Date.now() internally so it stays deterministic under test. Write vitest unit tests asserting exact expected percentages against the fixed seed dataset from SKILL_002. Round consistently (e.g., 2 decimal places) and document the formula inline where the rounding choice is non-obvious.
acceptance_criteria: calculateUptime(downtimeMs, totalPeriodMs) returns the exact expected percentage for fixed numeric inputs
Function signature accepts explicit/injectable timestamps and performs no internal Date.now() or new Date() calls
Unit test suite asserts exact expected uptime percentages against the fixed seed dataset for every seeded component

skills.name: Incidents REST API Endpoints
skills.capability: Exposes CRUD/read Express endpoints for incidents, including declaring incidents and reading full state-transition history.
skills.prompt_template: You are a backend API agent. Build Express routes for GET /api/incidents (list), GET /api/incidents/:id (detail with full stateHistory), and POST/PATCH endpoints to create incidents and transition their state, appending a timestamped entry to stateHistory on every transition. Reuse the schema from SKILL_001 and read from the seeded store from SKILL_002. Keep response serialization in a dedicated function so it is unit-testable independent of the HTTP layer.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/incidents returns the full list of seeded incidents on a fresh install
GET /api/incidents/:id returns a single incident including its complete stateHistory array
Response serializer includes id, title, severity, affectedComponents, summary, state, and stateHistory fields on every incident payload

skills.name: Components REST API Endpoints
skills.capability: Exposes CRUD/read Express endpoints for components including health state and computed uptime percentage.
skills.prompt_template: You are a backend API agent. Build Express routes for GET /api/components (list) and GET /api/components/:id (detail), returning each component's id, name, healthState, and uptimePercent computed via the uptime engine from SKILL_003. Reuse the schema from SKILL_001 and the seeded store from SKILL_002. Keep response serialization in a dedicated, independently testable function.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/components returns the full list of seeded components on a fresh install
GET /api/components/:id returns a single component including its current healthState and uptimePercent
Response serializer includes uptimePercent as a numeric field on every component payload

skills.name: Aggregate Stats Endpoint

testcases.name: MTTR in minutes for a single resolved incident
incidents this month filters by reference date's month

skills.capability: Computes and exposes aggregate operational stats — MTTR, open incident count, incidents this month, and overall uptime — via a single stats endpoint.
skills.prompt_template: You are a backend stats agent. Implement pure helper functions computeMTTR(incidents), computeOpenCount(incidents), and computeIncidentsThisMonth(incidents, referenceDate) that take arrays of incidents (and an injectable reference date, never Date.now()) and return deterministic numeric results. Wire these plus the overall uptime engine from SKILL_003 into a GET /api/stats endpoint that aggregates across the incidents and components APIs from SKILL_004 and SKILL_005.
acceptance_criteria: computeMTTR returns the exact mean time-to-resolution in minutes for a fixed array of resolved incidents
computeOpenCount returns the exact count of incidents not in the resolved state for a fixed array
computeIncidentsThisMonth returns the exact count of incidents whose createdAt falls in the same month as a given reference date
GET /api/stats returns MTTR, open count, incidents this month, and overall uptime in a single response
